results.title: COP31: Advocates urge funders to double clean air money for Africa, Asia and Latin America by COP32
results.content: Clean air advocates at COP31 have urged philanthropic funders to double their annual support for air quality initiatives in Africa, Latin America and parts of Asia, warning that inadequate financing is undermining efforts to tackle pollution in some of the world's most affected regions. The advocates say the three regions, excluding China and India, currently receive a combined US$8.3 million annually in philanthropic funding for clean air work. They want that amount increased to about US$16 million a year, with more resources directed towards locally led monitoring systems, research and the use of air quality data in policymaking. The call was made during a session on financing clean air in the Global South, co-hosted by Sustenta Honduras and Clean Energy Nepal in Antalya, Türkiye, on November 13.

results.title: Ghana Chamber of Clean Energy commends BPA, First Sky on completion of Yendi solar plant
results.content: The Ghana Chamber of Clean Energy (GCCE) has commended the Bui Power Authority (BPA) and First Sky Limited following the completion of a 50-megawatt-peak (MWp) solar photovoltaic power plant at Galgu in the Yendi Municipality of the Northern Region. In a statement issued on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, the Chamber described the project as a significant step in Ghana’s efforts to expand renewable energy generation and strengthen local participation in the clean energy industry. The project, developed by BPA and constructed by wholly Ghanaian-owned company First Sky Limited, has been completed, tested and connected to the national electricity grid.

results.title: Abu Jinapor questions NDC’s consistency over US$60.68m presidential jet
results.content: Former Lands and Natural Resources Minister Samuel Abu Jinapor has questioned the government’s decision to acquire a US$60.68 million presidential aircraft, accusing the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) of abandoning its earlier position on such expenditure. The Damongo MP says the acquisition of a new Falcon 6X executive jet raises questions about the party’s consistency, particularly given its opposition to proposals for a new presidential aircraft when it was in opposition.

results.title: One dead, tanker driver critically injured in fire outbreak at Amamprobi Junction

results.title: Ohene Kwame Frimpong agrees to extradition from the Netherlands to face US charges – Lawyer
results.content: The detained Member of Parliament for Asante Akim North, Ohene Kwame Frimpong, has agreed not to challenge his extradition from the Netherlands to the United States, a member of his legal team, Elvis Adu-Ameyaw, has said. Mr Adu-Ameyaw said the MP had decided to consent to the extradition to allow the allegations against him to be resolved. Ahead of the extradition hearing scheduled for Wednesday, November 18, 2026, the lawyer said his client was concerned about the plight of his constituents and Ghanaians generally. “Honourable Ohene Kwame Frimpong is concerned about the plight of his people. I am referring to the people of Asante Akim North and the Ghanaian people at large,” he said.

results.title: Data intelligence empowers African climate negotiators via first-of-its-kind Situation Room
results.content: The African Group of Negotiators (AGN) is leveraging data, technology and real-time intelligence to strengthen Africa’s participation and influence in international climate negotiations at COP31. The initiative, known as the African Situation Room, is designed to provide negotiators with timely information, evidence and analysis to support strategic decision-making throughout the complex UN climate negotiation process. With dozens of agenda items under consideration and relatively few delegates available to track the discussions, African negotiators face the challenge of monitoring multiple negotiation streams, analysing evolving draft texts and coordinating positions across thematic areas. The negotiation process is also highly fluid, with proposals, amendments and competing positions emerging continuously, making it increasingly difficult for delegates to keep pace with developments.

results.title: COP31: Ghana demands funds to repair Africa’s mining-scarred lands, triple adaptation finance
results.content: Ghana has demanded that countries which grew rich on Africa’s minerals pay to restore the rivers, forests and lands damaged by mining, and deliver on a pledge to triple finance for climate adaptation by 2035. Speaking at the Africa Day Ministerial Segment of COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, on 14 November, Ghana’s Minister for Environment, Science and Technology, Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, said the repair money must be “written into any agreement for Africa’s minerals.” “Those who built their prosperity on this exploitation have not treated its repair as a moral imperative. They must. Africa is not here to beg. We are here to demand a moral obligation,” she said.

results.content: Ghana has proposed six demands that African environment ministers should take into the high-level talks at the UN climate conference, COP31, in Antalya, Türkiye, and urged them to speak with one voice. results.title: Who gets to tell Ghana’s story on the cedi? An open letter to the Bank of Ghana on the Heritage series
results.content: Dear colleagues at the Bank of Ghana, I write to you as a fellow practitioner. In more than 20 years in PR, including my time in banking as Head of Corporate Communications, I have learnt what it feels like to spend months preparing for a launch and then find, within hours, that the public is having a different conversation from the one you planned. I want this launch to work for the Bank and for the people who use the cedi every day. I tell my public relations students that PR should also stand for People’s Reactions. We used to assess a launch by the press release and the front pages the next morning. The question I ask now is what people do after you publish or post. By that measure, the first few days of the Heritage Series have been difficult. What went right?
